interface.name: denial_orientation_manager_v1

description.summary: an application window's preferred display orientation

interface.description:
On Denial's mobile shell the display follows the orientation sensor and the user's rotation lock. An application toplevel may ask for an orientation instead, as an Android activity does with its requested orientation: a game that only works in landscape turns the display to landscape while it is the front window, whatever the lock says.
The shell honours the request of the front application window only, and never while the home or lock screen is shown. Desktop layout is unaffected. The request is a preference: the shell may ignore it, for example on a display that does not rotate.

entry.name: invalid_orientation
entry.summary: the orientation is not a value of the orientation enum

entry.name: unspecified
entry.summary: follow the rotation lock, or the sensor when unlocked

entry.name: landscape
entry.summary: landscape, always on the same side

entry.name: sensor_landscape
entry.summary: landscape, the side chosen by the sensor

entry.name: sensor
entry.summary: follow the sensor, even when the rotation is locked

entry.name: locked
entry.summary: keep the orientation the display has now

request.name: set_orientation

description.summary: set the preferred orientation of a toplevel

request.description: Set the orientation the display should take while this application toplevel is the front window. It takes effect immediately rather than on wl_surface.commit, may be sent at any time and lasts for the wl_surface lifetime, including unmap and remap, until it is set again. Destroying this manager does not undo it. Surfaces that are not toplevels are ignored.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Orientations already set remain in effect.
